end.summary:
Practised representing 11–20 as one ten-bundle and loose ones.
Saanvi identified 13 as one bundle and three loose sticks once.
They initially counted the ten-bundle as one object when finding the total.
They confused the ten in 15 and 17 with one, then identified it as ten after prompting.
They wrote 41 for fourteen and later identified 4 as the ones digit, but did not write the corrected numeral.
end.parentNote: Saanvi practised showing teen numbers with one bundle of ten and loose ones, and locating the ones digit on the right. Using the phrase “one ten plus four ones” helped them say fourteen as fourteen, but the bundle-counting and digit-order mix-ups were still present at the end. At home, build teen numbers with one group of ten and loose objects, then say and write “one ten plus ___ ones” together.
